caption: R7 150 of my salary goes to people I owe before I buy anything for myself. How long did it take you to clear yours?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R29 500
p/m salary
Living in Nelspruit
slides.body:
Female, 30
Single, no kids
Job: Retail assistant manager
Net salary: R29 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: I moved here after the store transfer. Not glamorous, but it's five minutes from the till.

slides.title: Credit card
slides.body: I know exactly what I bought with this. I don't love remembering.

slides.title: Store account
slides.includes: Edgars and Foschini combined, R9 800 owing
slides.body: It felt like nothing at R299 a month per account. It's R1 450 together.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R64 000 balance, 24% interest, 24 months left, taken for a car repair and a family funeral in the same month
slides.body: Two emergencies, one loan. I don't regret it. I do watch the interest.

slides.title: Takeaways & coffee
slides.includes: Till-side coffee, Friday lunch with the team, delivery on closing shifts
slides.body: I guessed R500. It was R1 050. Closing shifts make you buy things.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Groceries, petrol & insurance, medical aid, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, electricity, black tax
slides.body: R12 800 that isn't debt and isn't rent. It's the only part of this I can actually move.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R29 500. R7 150 of that went to the card, the store account and the loan. At this pace the store account clears in 7 months, the card in 11, the loan in 24.

slides.title: I stopped avoiding what I owe
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

Seeing the three debt repayments added up on one screen was worse, and more useful, than any of them alone.

No bank login needed.
